findings.invariant: The parser/reference grammar/issuer-key-use map deciding whether a supplied chain is verified is a fixed code-pinned trusted boundary, not caller-selected data or behavior.
findings.worked_counterexample: A caller supplies a registry whose validator accepts an extra application key or whose reference grammar omits a required IssuanceBasisRef/PIS/PCE edge. Canonical, correctly signed bytes pass that supplied validator. V2 neither requires schema_registry to be one exact internal object/blob identity nor rejects a different mapping, so a conforming constructor can return an opaque verified chain whose closure is weaker than ADR-0125.
findings.consequence: Caller-selected schema policy can downgrade default-deny and transitive-link validation, producing materially wrong verified-chain results. Opaqueness/no effects prevents immediate capture but does not make an incorrect verifier result acceptable.
findings.required_disposition: Do not authorize RED. Remove schema_registry from the public constructor or require exact identity to one internal immutable code-pinned registry whose complete entries and validator/dependency blob pins are specified. Keyring, clock, and revocations are the only injected trusted seams. Repeat Phase 0.

findings.invariant: Each advertised action/final profile is finite and implementable only when every reachable schema, reference kind/role, validator, and dependency is exhaustively enumerated and pinned before verification.
findings.worked_counterexample: An action profile reaches RootPublicationReceipt.v1 through required root PIS. ADR-0125 requires that receipt to validate its exact G1/G2 DatasetCaptureAuthorization and issuance basis. 0039 requires root publication authorization/receipt/PIS closure but does not name the DatasetCaptureAuthorization schema/version, closed grammar, signer/key-use, basis/ref grammar, or validator/dependency blob pin. Broad phrases such as 'all ... recursively referenced object' and 'fixed owner policy' leave the same missing finite table. Treating an omission as external refuses a profile-required dependency; admitting it makes validation invented or dynamic.
findings.consequence: The closure cannot both be exact/default-deny and verify the advertised complete profiles. It either rejects otherwise valid profiles at a mandatory omitted dependency or makes closure semantics implementation-defined, so Packet 3 is insufficiently specified for RED.
findings.required_disposition: Do not authorize RED. Publish a finite registry table for every reachable schema, including root-publication authorization and policy/basis dependencies, with exact schema/version, key grammar, named digest, issuer/key-use, typed refs, and code/dependency blob pin. Profiles must reference that closed table only. Repeat Phase 0.

validated_design_points: A supplied finite byte request plus cycle/self/future/unreachable-extra refusal gives a sound finite traversal shape once a complete fixed registry exists.
